correctness.rationale: The valuation identity follows from Legendre factorial valuations, not empirical fitting. The exact block partition proves (5) with every term. The borrow-count identity proves the required high-valuation annihilation. Root-of-unity blocks give power-saving cancellation over arbitrary real cutoffs, implying true natural densities. The mixture counts use exact numbers of low-digit classes. Sharpness considers all p, including k=1. The standalone exact checker validates factorial, carry and literal product valuations and modular histograms for finite ranges. No inference from finitely many tests is used.

originality.rationale: Lagarias–Mehta Theorem 5.1 covers the pointwise prime valuations of full Pascal-row products and is fully credited. The checked paper does not formulate the universal prime-power residue densities, conditional uniformity, exact finite-block histograms, or sharp digit compression. Their derivation adds a digit-block identity, nontrivial character-sum cancellation for all cutoffs, and a prime-adic mixture argument. The companion reduced-Farey paper, finite OEIS tables and nearest semantic archive results do not imply this full set by their stated conclusions. There remains a real historical-priority risk from an implicit general automatic-sequence theorem.
residual_risks: The 2014 pointwise identity mathematically determines W_p(n), and the density theorem might be recognized as an implicit consequence in broader digital-sum theory.
Semantic search and accessible papers cannot rule out unindexed early results or an unpublished equivalent.
No independent referee or formal proof assistant has certified the analytic argument.

value.rationale: Prime-power residue statistics of the prime valuations of full Pascal-row/Farey products form a natural local arithmetic invariant. The nonuniform universal mass law for all p,k answers a complete distribution question, with conditional fiber structure, a rigorous power-saving and exact finite-block enumerator. The optimal low-digit threshold gives a natural sharp computational arithmetic boundary. The result is more than a routine numerical table or a restatement of the existing pointwise expression.
